blocks.title: Your agent gets a phone number
body: Connect a managed number or your own carrier, with transfers, hold, and keypad input built in. On outbound calls, AMD tells you who picked up: a person, a voicemail, or a screening assistant.
Build an inbound support line, a callback flow, or routing based on who answers.
blocks.label: Telephony · AMD

blocks.title: You see the words as they're spoken
body: Hear gives your app a live view of the call, updating the transcript as the caller speaks and marking each utterance final. About 200 ms to the first partial, measured in-region.
Build live captions, or index recorded calls for search.
blocks.label: Hear

blocks.title: Build the agent around your own functions
body: Connect your instructions, knowledge, and application tools, so the agent can check an order, find an appointment, and respond with the result during the call.
Configure and test it in Agents, or build directly with the Omni SDK.
blocks.label: Omni · Agents

blocks.title: Your text becomes the voice they hear
body: Choose a stock, cloned, or designed voice, then stream spoken responses in the audio format your app needs. Speech starts within about 53 ms, measured in-region.
Add spoken replies to your app, generate phone prompts, or feed your existing pipeline.
blocks.label: Speak

blocks.title: The call ends with data your app can use
body: Receive a summary, a disposition, the next step, and structured fields you define. Deliver the result through a webhook or a supported integration when the call ends.
Capture booking details, create a CRM note, or pass a summary into your workflow.

blocks.title: Review each finding alongside its rule
body: Submit calls against your rule packs and retrieve scorecards with cited findings, redactions, and a tamper-evident audit hash. Works on calls from any stack.
Build a review queue, flag specific findings, or bring evaluations into your dashboard.

sections.title: Three lessons from a billion calls
sections.label: Our point of view

blocks.title: Phone audio needs its own training data
body: Accents, noise, and compression come with the call. Hear is tuned for 8 kHz narrowband audio, so it transcribes what your phone line delivers.
blocks.label: Hear

blocks.title: Turn-taking has to be built into the model
body: Hearing, thinking, and speaking operate as a single model, so it stops when the caller does and replies at a human pace.
blocks.label: Omni
blocks.metricNote: from the caller stopping to the reply starting

blocks.title: One system has to run the whole call
body: The line, the conversation, and the notes run together, so there is one place to debug and one bill to read.

sections.title: Keep your stack. Nothing you run today has to go.
items: On the OpenAI SDK? Change the base URL and the key. Speech and transcription work the same.
On Twilio, Plivo, or your own carrier? Keep it. Or take a managed number in the US or India.
On LiveKit or Pipecat? PyAI drops in as the voice, and your loop stays yours.
On HubSpot, Salesforce, or Zendesk? The call notes write into them.

examples.label: Python
examples.code:
# before
client = OpenAI()

# after
client = OpenAI(
  base_url="https://api.pyai.com/v1",
  api_key=os.environ["PYAI_API_KEY"])

# everything else stays
client.audio.speech.create(
  model="pyai-speak", voice="stock_ava_en_us",
  input="Hi, thanks for calling.")

examples.label: TypeScript
cURL
examples.code:
# same request shape as OpenAI's
curl https://api.pyai.com/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PYAI_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"pyai-speak",
       "voice":"stock_ava_en_us",
       "input":"Hi, thanks for calling."}' \
  -o speech.mp3

sections.title: For the people who have to sign it off
sections.label: Security and compliance

blocks.title: Your data stays on your servers
body: Your knowledge base never moves. PyAI reads what each answer needs, at the moment it needs it.

blocks.title: Keys never reach the browser
body: Each key is scoped to one project and lives on your server. Browsers get short-lived tokens.

blocks.title: Recording stays off until you turn it on
body: Recording is off by default. You set the consent line, retention period, and regional rules per call.

blocks.title: Every reviewed call keeps its evidence
body: Trace stores the rule, the finding, and a tamper-evident hash together, ready for an audit.

sections.title: Before you get a key
sections.label: FAQ
intro: Anything else, write to us. A person reads it, usually the same day.

blocks.title: Is this AtomsAI or PyAI?
body: PyAI is the infrastructure layer of AtomsAI, with its own console, docs, and pricing. You build on the same layer our products do.

blocks.title: Do I need your products to use it?
body: No. Bring your own app, carrier, and CRM.

blocks.title: How fast is it on a real call?
body: About 390 ms from the caller finishing a sentence to hearing the reply, measured in-region. Not an SLA.

blocks.title: Does my OpenAI code work?
body: For speech and transcription, yes, after changing the base URL and the key. Real-time agents use PyAI's own connection, which the SDKs handle.

blocks.title: Which languages?
body: Twenty in all. Twelve have voice agents, nineteen have text-to-speech, eleven have speech-to-text.

blocks.title: Where do I start?
body: Get a free sandbox key, or tell us what you're building and we'll start there.

closing.title: Get a key, or get in touch.
